intro.title: The WebP vs. JPG Compatibility Dilemma
intro.p1: WebP is the modern standard for high-speed web images, offering superior compression. However, this efficiency creates compatibility issues. Many legacy systems, older image viewers, and professional desktop editors still struggle to open or display WebP files correctly.
intro.p2: Our **WebP to JPG Converter** bridges this gap. It instantly transforms your optimized WebP assets into the universally recognized JPEG format. Whether for PowerPoint presentations, strict CMS uploads, or legacy device viewing, this tool ensures your images work everywhere.
intro.p3: Engineered for quality, our tool performs a true deep-decode and re-encode cycle. unlike generic screenshot-based converters, we preserve color profiles and visual integrity, delivering a high-fidelity JFIF-compliant JPEG.

story.title: Why Compatibility Matters
story.p1: The need for universal access often drives the switch from WebP to JPG. While WebP dominates the web, it often fails in offline or legacy environments.

sub_1.title: The 'Walled Garden' of Software
sub_1.p1: Desktop ecosystems have been slow to adopt WebP. Trying to use WebP in older Office or Photoshop versions often triggers 'invalid file format' errors. Converting to JPG removes this friction.
sub_1.p2: Social media uploaders are also strict. By validating your assets as strict JPGs before upload, you avoid backend rejection or poor server-side re-compression.

sub_2.title: The Alpha Channel Conflict
sub_2.p1: WebP supports transparency; JPG does not. Users are often confused when transparent logos turn black upon conversion. Our tool solves this by defaulting to a standard white matte.

sub_3.title: Regaining Control
sub_3.p1: Don't be locked into a format just because a website saved it that way. We give you the control to use your visual assets in any software or platform you choose.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Will converting WebP to JPG reduce quality?
faq.a1: JPG is a lossy format, so technically there is always some data change. However, our converter uses a high-quality setting (92-95%) which makes the visual difference imperceptible to the human eye.
faq.q2: Why did my file size increase?
faq.a2: WebP is an ultra-compressed format designed for the web. JPG is an older standard. To maintain the same visual quality, a JPG file often needs to be 20-50% larger than its WebP counterpart.
faq.a3: The tool will convert the first frame of an animated WebP into a static high-resolution JPG image. JPG does not support animation.
faq.q4: Is this tool free for commercial use?
faq.a4: Yes, our WebP to JPG converter is 100% free for both personal and commercial use. There are no watermarks or usage limits.
faq.q5: Can I convert on my iPhone?
faq.a5: Absolutely. Modern iOS versions support WebP, and our tool works directly in Safari to let you save JPGs to your Photos app.
faq.q6: What happens to the transparent background?
faq.a6: Since JPG doesn't support transparency, we automatically fill transparent areas with correct white background, making it suitable for documents.
faq.q7: Do you simply rename the file extension?
faq.a7: No. Renaming .webp to .jpg corrupts the file. We perform a full transcoding process, decoding the pixels and re-encoding them as a valid JPEG image.
faq.q8: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a8: We support files up to 10MB, which covers almost all web-resolution images and most high-definition photography.
faq.q9: Do I need to install any software?
faq.a9: No, this is a fully cloud-native web application. It runs entirely in your browser without any plugins or downloads.
faq.a10: For most images, the process is near-instantaneous (under 1 second). Larger high-res photos may take 2-3 seconds depending on your device speed.
